pairs.difference: A: the night-blue sky stays cool behind pink, orange and green neon, and the motel wall keeps a lilac tone beside its yellow windows. B: the saloon's grey siding and pale false front fall into peach and tan masses in the lens, the same brown as the wood and sand. Subject chroma (0.048) is just under the real floor, and warm share is 0.711 with only the sky and red door frame breaking it.
pairs.fix: Keep the grey siding and pale facade a cool neutral grey-white with blue-violet shadows. Do not tint them tan or peach; keep the warm color only in the wood beams and sand.

pairs.difference: A: the steel horseshoe stays a true cool grey with small gold rivets and lands as a muted grey mass on the green; subject chroma and hue count are below the real range, but the local color is believable. B: the neck pillow is pure blue from light side to shadow, with almost no neutral, set straight against loud pink. Only a thin violet trace appears at the bottom edge.
pairs.fix: Make the pillow a slightly dusty, soft fabric blue with pale grey-blue highlights and violet-navy shadows, not one pure electric blue.

pairs.difference: A: three clear masses of cobalt pot, pink wall and orange wood, with white dots and a white rim as rest. B: the sneakers scatter lime, teal, magenta, orange and violet accents across blue uppers and the sole, reaching 5.49 hue families, above the real range. There is no single accent, and background chroma sits below the real range.
pairs.fix: Limit the sneakers to one blue plus white soles and one accent color. Remove the rainbow laces and multicolor sole trim.

pairs.difference: A: the mill keeps grey metal blades, natural brown wood and one red tail vane as the accent; sky and grass are loud and shadow chroma is low at 0.564. B: a pure cobalt door meets orange-pushed wood trim, with pink, yellow and orange flowers and a full wall of green ivy. The wood reads orange rather than brown, and there is little neutral rest beyond the small cream wall strip.
pairs.fix: Paint the door frame a natural mid-brown wood, soften the door to a slightly greyed blue, and keep the wreath to two flower colors.

pairs.difference: A: grey-brown driftwood stays a muted natural color on purple, and its sand shadow turns violet, a rich related shift like the real glove's shadow. Subject chroma (0.0515) is below the real range. B: the cart's red is pure and even, and the gold and blue background are at full strength, so only the awning white and paving rest the eye.
pairs.fix: Deepen the cart's red into a slightly crimson body with plum shadows, and make the gold trim a quieter brass with less yellow-orange.

pairs.difference: A: table, rail, cover and shadows all run orange to red, and the hedge is pulled yellow-olive in the lens. Warm share (0.758) and shadow chroma (1.751) are above the real range, so the shadows are orange-red everywhere. B: a dark teal-grey lamp on cyan is nearly one hue, also outside the range at the low end, but its dark neutral and muted glass give the color a rest.
pairs.fix: Use a paler natural wood table, cool green hedges and white pages. Make shadows muted violet-brown instead of orange-red.

pairs.difference: A: the planter is a flat pure red-orange, even in wood that should show brown, at subject chroma 0.1772 above the real range; the fence is pushed orange too. B: the green pack against a red ground is loud (background 0.1701), but brown leather straps and grey buckles give it believable local color.
pairs.fix: Paint the planter a slightly weathered barn red with visible brown wood tone and darker wine shadows. Keep the fence a pale natural grey-brown.

pairs.difference: A: the cart, rivets, ore and sand all sit in one copper-orange family, and shadows fall to plain brown with low kept chroma (0.553). No cool or neutral appears on the hero. B: cream parchment, red ribbon and gold seal on blue have clear roles, and the blue table keeps rich shadows at 1.419, slightly above the real range.
pairs.fix: Make the cart body grey-blue iron with cool violet shadows, and keep the gold ore as the only warm yellow on the object. Make the sand paler and less orange.

pairs.difference: A: the scarf is pure red with deep red folds on cyan, a loud pair at subject chroma 0.2165, but the hue roles are clean and the badge adds one gold accent. B: the harmonica's grey steel falls to tan and brown masses in the lens, so orange has soaked into the metal. Warm share is 0.998, above the real range, and it matches how generated computers turned cream in the lessons.
pairs.fix: Keep the harmonica steel a cool neutral grey with blue-grey shadows and clean white highlights. Do not reflect the orange background into the metal.

pairs.difference: A: the card faces stay cool lilac-white and hold as neutral in the lens against the orange ground, like the real computer's cool side, though the wood's warmth and strong shadow chroma are extreme. B: the ball's white panels turn peach and pale yellow, its shadow is full red-orange on the sand, and the sand itself is orange, so the whole card is pulled warm.
pairs.fix: Keep the ball's white panels a clean cool white with pale blue-grey shading. Make its sand shadow a muted violet, and make the sand paler and less orange.

pairs.difference: A: pure yellow star on pure violet with background chroma 0.2635, above the real range. The star is a single flat yellow mass in the lens with little hue shift and no neutral anywhere. B: crimson box, tan cushion, gold medal and blue ribbon on cyan use more hues (5.43, above range), but the cushion's muted tan gives real rest.
pairs.fix: Quiet the purple background to a deeper, slightly dusty violet. Move the star's shading from yellow into amber and brown-orange, and darken the star's side faces toward ochre.

pairs.difference: A: a red-brown piano on pale blue stripes, with white keys that stay cool in the lens. B: pink roses and green leaves on pale pink stripes, with stems and shade falling to dull brown. Both backgrounds are under the real chroma range and shadow retention is close to the floor on both, so hue and chroma give no reason to choose.

pattern: Generated cards are given away first by what happens to neutrals. Whites, greys and steel soak up the warm background and turn cream, peach or tan, where real cards keep them cool with blue-violet shadow sides. Next is warm bias: wood goes orange and shadows go orange-red or plain brown instead of a related violet or plum. Generated cards also tend to hold one hue at full strength on the hero with little neutral rest, or scatter extra accent hues, rather than one local color and one accent. These calls are mostly low confidence, because the pairs show different objects and several real-looking neutral subjects also fall outside the measured ranges.
